contract.current_promise: Future changes remain backward-compatible with 0.1 or use a new version number; M4A owns supported-version ranges, negotiation, migration, and rejection policy.

optional_sections: artifact: module and module metadata for independent products
current.section_order: optional artifact: module and module metadata, constants, names, main, zero or more function sections, optional debug_sources, optional debug_locations, optional debug_ranges
current.parser_policy: Rust parsing is strict: artifact kind, module fields, dependency markers, required sections, sequential references, instruction shapes, debug references and ranges, and trailing/unknown sections are rejected.
current.formatter_policy: Rust dump canonicalizes either linked cdbc 0.1 programs or module products to the same text representation emitted by C++.
current.debug_policy: Debug metadata is additive and optional; source/function/instruction indexes are artifact-local, debug_ranges use source-local half-open byte intervals, and line and column values are one-based.

evolution_decisions.current_state: The cdbc 0.1 envelope distinguishes linked programs by the absence of an artifact declaration and independent products with artifact: module; the module CLI emits one product per graph node and Rust dump/run enforce the distinction.
evolution_decisions.named_consumer: C++ BytecodeTextEmitter, C++ module emitter, and Rust format parser/CLI
evolution_decisions.rationale: Independent products need a strict non-executable envelope, but their bytecode sections remain compatible with the existing cdbc 0.1 family and parser.

revisit.condition: Change only if linking, runtime compatibility, or a concrete transport requires a successor version or separate family.

evolution_decisions.current_state: Optional debug_sources, debug_locations, and debug_ranges sections are emitted, strictly parsed, and used by the Rust VM and module linker for source-aware runtime metadata; each emitted range is paired with a location and uses source-local half-open byte offsets; M4B-DEBUG-002 adds an optional canonical source-to-module identity field.
evolution_decisions.named_consumer: Rust VM runtime diagnostics and debugger-oriented M4B work
evolution_decisions.rationale: The additive metadata covers current source-mapped runtime diagnostics and preserves complete source ranges for future debugger consumers without changing core execution sections.

revisit.condition: Extend metadata only when a named debugger/runtime consumer requires a field not expressible by the current sparse mappings.

evolution_decisions.current_state: The Rust parser is strict and rejects an unexpected section instead of silently skipping it.
evolution_decisions.rationale: Strict rejection protects the current canonical parser/formatter contract and prevents an older VM from silently misinterpreting new semantics.

revisit.condition: Change only with an explicit versioned forward-compatibility policy and parser tests for unknown sections.

evolution_decisions.current_state: The artifact does not declare a target triple, VM identity, or runtime feature set; the current compiler and Rust VM are the only named consumer pair.
evolution_decisions.named_consumer: M4A compatibility validator, if multi-runtime or cross-target transport is introduced
evolution_decisions.rationale: No current transport or consumer needs to select among runtimes or targets, so adding an unconsumed field would create speculative ABI surface.

revisit.condition: A second runtime, target, or artifact transport requires deterministic compatibility rejection or selection.

evolution_decisions.current_state: The current version has one fixed opcode/native capability set and no negotiation handshake.
evolution_decisions.rationale: Capability bits without a consumer-defined negotiation or rejection rule would be metadata without semantics.

revisit.condition: A compatible extension needs feature discovery while preserving a supported 0.1 reader/writer path.

evolution_decisions.current_state: Independent module products serialize the ModuleGraph canonical path as identity, retain display/canonical paths, entry ordering, and dependency target identities; import-aware debug source tables also retain canonical source-to-module identity.
evolution_decisions.named_consumer: M3B module product emitter/linker, M4B debug metadata, and Rust artifact validator
evolution_decisions.rationale: Per-module products must be linkable across independent files without treating snapshot-local numeric module IDs as persistent identities.

revisit.condition: Revise if a linker or cross-build cache requires a stronger identity/hash contract.

evolution_decisions.current_state: The contract is a line-oriented UTF-8 file; no streaming, concatenation, embedded transport, or binary consumer exists.
evolution_decisions.rationale: A new framing layer would add format and implementation cost without a concrete transport requirement.

revisit.condition: A named transport requires bounded records, random access, binary encoding, or corruption-resilient framing.

evolution_decisions.current_state: The current artifact has no embedded digest or signature; local tests compare complete text files and the Rust parser validates structure.
evolution_decisions.named_consumer: M4A artifact transport/cache or security validator, if introduced
evolution_decisions.rationale: Structural parsing and repository golden comparison cover the current local workflow; an integrity field needs a defined trust boundary and failure policy.

revisit.condition: Artifacts cross an untrusted transport or are cached/shared where authenticity or corruption detection is a stated requirement.

evolution_decisions.current_state: No successor version or negotiation range is selected; the parser accepts exactly cdbc 0.1 and rejects other family/version headers before execution.
evolution_decisions.named_consumer: M4A compatibility matrix, migration/rejection policy, and version-aware Rust parser
evolution_decisions.rationale: A breaking artifact change would need a new version, but M0.5B finds no current requirement that justifies selecting one now.

revisit.condition: A selected artifact/runtime change cannot remain a compatible extension of 0.1 and has a concrete producer/consumer migration plan.

successor_decision.decision: No cdbc successor is required or selected at M0.5B.
successor_decision.rationale: M0.5B selected no successor because the current 0.1 envelope covered the linked compiler/VM pair. M3B later introduced independent module products as a compatible artifact-kind extension, without selecting a successor version. M4A remains authorized to select a successor if a later compatibility requirement proves that a 0.1-compatible extension is insufficient.
triggers: module linking requiring fields that cannot remain a compatible cdbc 0.1 extension
a named transport/security requirement that cannot fit a compatible extension

invalid_input_policy.reference_corpus: tests/malformed_cases.json cdbc mutations plus vm-rs format unit tests

m4a_compatibility.question: How should the current cdbc 0.1 artifact family be accepted, rejected, and validated before execution?
m4a_compatibility.decision: Keep exact cdbc 0.1 support for linked programs and independent module products, reject other family/version headers and unsupported native capabilities, and validate every serialized cross-reference before dump, link, or VM execution.

compatibility_matrix.dump: accept after structural and reference validation
accept after structural, reference, and module-envelope validation
compatibility_matrix.link: accept only when the complete product set validates

validation_contract: constant number literals must parse as finite f64 values
constant, name, function, and register references must address their tables
jump targets may equal the instruction count but may not exceed it
debug location arrays must match instruction counts and retain parser range checks
native_call names must belong to the cdbc 0.1 native capability set
module identities, entry metadata, dependency targets, and insertion offsets must validate before linking

successor_decision.rationale: The current compiler/Rust VM pair needs stronger validation but no new opcode, value layout, target, transport, or negotiation capability. A successor version would add migration surface without a named consumer.
successor_decision.revisit: Select a successor only when a breaking runtime/artifact change cannot remain a compatible 0.1 extension.

m4a_compatibility.migration: The existing cdbc 0.1 core emitter, canonical section structure, and runtime behavior remain unchanged. M4B-DEBUG-002 later adds an optional source-to-module field to import-aware debug source entries without changing the version. The Rust parser performs centralized validation before returning an artifact; existing linked and module-product paths retain their commands and rejection policy.
m4a_compatibility.old_path_deletion_condition: Do not remove cdbc 0.1 readers or emitters. An older path may be retired only after a separately versioned successor has a complete matrix, migration/rejection policy, deprecation period, and canonical evidence.
